entries.subject: Veverka 1996 Galileo dimensions
entries.finding: The measured full dimensions 1.6 × 1.4 × 1.2 km define a smooth ellipsoid. This is an envelope, not a recovered crater mesh, and the reference radius is its computed volume-equivalent radius.

entries.subject: Galileo resolved Dactyl observations
entries.finding: Native SSI data and evaluated spacecraft pointing are retained, but the fixed-ellipsoid orientation is sensitive to the sampled outline. Celmis error is 12.70 pixels using the left limb, 0.23 after adding the lower cap, and 18.48 with both caps. Each fit is selected without Celmis; the development check is not a fresh blind validation. No photographic lens is enabled.
entries.revisitWhen: Actual SSI products and their camera/shape relation pass independent surface registration for the selected geometry.

entries.subject: Stooke shape collection membership
entries.finding: The historical inventory explicitly includes Ida but not Dactyl. The primary mesh cannot substitute for its moon; this collection-specific result does not rule out another Dactyl release.
entries.revisitWhen: A Dactyl-specific numerical model is identified with its native frame and source attribution.

entries.subject: Generic Celestia Dactyl texture
entries.finding: The retained source-selection record excludes a generic rock texture because it is not observed Dactyl imagery.
entries.revisitWhen: An observational Dactyl texture with traceable native data and controlled registration replaces the generic material.

entries.subject: Belton/Petit encounter and stability orbit constraints
entries.finding: The papers constrain encounter orbit families but not a unique current phase. The displayed candidate conic uses a=82.3 km and e=0.15 from the retained Celestia record; its plane, periapsis, synchronous orientation and zero mean anomaly at the scene epoch are explicitly approximate.

entries.subject: Galileo SSI i1578 IR-8890 exposure
entries.finding: The smaller complete IR-8890 disk remains a candidate second view. The recovered telemetry CK has no zero-tolerance coverage at this exposure's shutter-center SCET. An exploratory transfer using preliminary label pointing, approximate range and assumed fixed orientation was not controlled surface evidence. The calibrated-image label was inspected; calibrated pixels remain unexamined.
entries.revisitWhen: A Dactyl camera-to-shape binding is available and the resolved image features support a meaningful independent check.

entries.subject: Galileo SSI i2278 CLEAR exposure
entries.finding: Original VICAR proves the FITS vertical inversion and the diagnostic includes SSI radial distortion. Additional lower and upper outline crossings change the selected orientation despite limb RMS below 0.60 pixels. The apparently successful lower-cap fit does not survive the upper-cap check. This is an unresolved camera/shape interpretation, not evidence that a faithful registered area is impossible.
entries.revisitWhen: The exposure has a source-backed Dactyl body-frame camera solution or distributed surface controls with independent holdouts for the existing ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Galileo SSI i2700 CLEAR exposure as the primary photographic view
entries.finding: The decoded detector contains only fragments of Dactyl at its left edge. The nominal finer resolution does not supply a complete disk or distributed interior controls, so this frame is excluded as the primary surface view. A future use of a valid edge fragment is not ruled out.
entries.revisitWhen: A separately qualified camera solution and detector-quality mask demonstrate a useful, registered fragment in this exposure.

entries.subject: Reconstructed Galileo 1993 scan-platform CK
entries.finding: The shared reader now evaluates platform -77001 in B1950 at i2278 shutter center, 1993-08-28T16:47:49.956Z. It agrees with native CSPICE N0067 to 5.7e-11 per matrix element. The reconstructed J2000 boresight differs from the preliminary label by about 191 native pixels. i1578 and i2700 have no zero-tolerance coverage at their shutter centers in this kernel. This is evaluated spacecraft pointing, not a Dactyl body-frame solution.

entries.subject: Mission mips_010314.tpc as a Dactyl body-orientation source
entries.finding: The retrieved, retained mission PCK contains no Dactyl or BODY2431011 assignment. It contains Ida parameters, which cannot establish the moon frame. This is a file-specific finding; it does not establish that PDS lacks Dactyl geometry.
entries.revisitWhen: A Dactyl-specific orientation record with epoch, reference frame and selected-shape axis binding is located.

entries.subject: PDS Thomas shape-model collection image-control tables
entries.finding: The inspected directory inventory includes the Ida image-control table, but no Dactyl-specific model or image-control table. The Ida table cannot control Dactyl. This finding is restricted to the examined release inventory.
entries.revisitWhen: A Dactyl-specific numerical model or image-control table is identified with its observation and frame bindings.

entries.subject: USGS Dactyl named-feature photograph and center points
entries.finding: Acmon (-39,138E) and Celmis (-46,220E) are confirmed by the current Gazetteer and Belton 1996 overview Table III. Analyst detector picks have about one-pixel uncertainty. Fitting the limb plus Acmon fails on withheld Celmis; selecting another solution after inspecting Celmis removes its independence. The two centers still do not supply a distributed control network.
entries.revisitWhen: An independently bound camera solution can predict the named centers, or additional distributed source controls permit disjoint fitting and validation.

entries.subject: Veverka et al. 1996 full paper camera and shape details
entries.finding: The publisher opens a 12-page full PDF. The first page and part of Table I were read in the browser, but modeled views and remaining tables are still unexamined: subsequent access reached human verification. ADS legacy routes, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex did not provide a downloadable alternative. This paper is partly retrieved, not fully reviewed.
entries.revisitWhen: A readable full paper or author-repository copy permits inspection of the observation geometry, axis convention, tables and figures.

entries.subject: GO_0016 VICAR detector orientation and SSI shutter timing
entries.finding: The original 2278R.IMG and native label are retained. All 640000 DN samples agree exactly with vertically reversed i2278 FITS rows; 316986 disagree without reversal. Mission CATSTAT distinguishes frame-start SCLK from shutter-center SCET. Use original zero-based detector coordinates and SCET, with no extra half-exposure offset.

entries.subject: Five neighboring SSI frames as additional Dactyl interior controls
entries.finding: Retrieved and decoded original 2178, 2300, 2378, 2452 and 2600 VICAR frames and labels. Full-detector inspection found sky/readout artifacts in four and a large Ida limb in 2300, with no extra resolved Dactyl disk. This is a five-frame sample, not an exhaustive PDS inventory.
entries.revisitWhen: Another returned exposure is shown to contain resolved Dactyl interior features usable as independent surface controls.

entries.subject: Belton 1996 readable mission overview tables
entries.finding: Retrieved the complete overview PDF and examined the relevant narrative plus Tables I, IIA and III visually. Table III explicitly confirms east-positive Dactyl crater coordinates. Table IIA matches Ida geometry despite its combined Ida/Dactyl heading; it is not a Dactyl camera. Table I gives a spin-period lower bound, not a measured pole and phase.

entries.subject: Chapman author preprint as a complete Dactyl body frame
entries.finding: The readable author preprint constrains ellipsoid dimensions, the long axis to within about 15 degrees of Ida, and spin to greater than about 8 hours. These are useful orientation priors, not a measured complete camera-to-shape frame. Its illustrations were not present in the retrieved PostScript copy.
entries.revisitWhen: Published observation geometry or a distributed control solution binds the selected axes to the encounter camera without an assumed pole or spin phase.

entries.subject: i2278 bright-outline extent and orientation sensitivity
entries.finding: The serial experiment compares 17, 29 and 31 native threshold crossings with the same 576 pose starts, instrument distortion, fixed ellipsoid and Acmon control. The selected Celmis discrepancy changes from 12.70 to 0.23 to 18.48 native pixels. The cap samples are not equally spaced by arc length, and Celmis has been inspected during development.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-backed Dactyl frame and independent surface evidence resolve the sensitivity without selecting an outline subset for its desired crater fit.

entries.subject: Veverka 1996 spectral paper as Dactyl surface controls
entries.finding: All eleven pages, figures and the filter table were examined. Dactyl has disk-averaged spectra; the mapped figures are Ida. This paper does not supply Dactyl image-specific body orientation or distributed surface controls.
entries.revisitWhen: A linked supplement or explicit Dactyl camera/control product is identified.

entries.subject: Oberst 1995 photogrammetry abstract as Dactyl surface controls
entries.finding: Both pages of extracted text were examined. The 96-point network and more than 5000 matched points are explicitly Ida surface points. The Dactyl paragraph proposes ephemeris work and publishes no Dactyl surface coordinates or camera-to-body solution.
entries.revisitWhen: A subsequent release publishes Dactyl-specific surface controls or observation geometry.

entries.subject: Generic pck00011 as a Dactyl body-orientation source
entries.finding: Retrieved the complete generic pck00011 file, read its introduction/body inventory and searched every byte for Dactyl and 2431011. Neither appears. This is a file-specific exclusion, not a claim that no archive contains Dactyl geometry.
entries.revisitWhen: A Dactyl-specific body frame with epoch and selected-shape axis binding is identified.
